host.note: dev laptop, shared with other work

methodology: Each scenario builds its own control plane slice (store, reconcile engine, embedded ingress) in the benchmark process and deploys a trivial fixture container on the local Docker engine.
The load generator runs on the same machine as the system under test, over loopback with TLS through the embedded ingress.

Request load is open loop: request i is scheduled at i / rate and latency is measured from that intended send time, so a stall is not hidden (coordinated omission). Ingress concurrency steps are closed loop and say so.
Percentiles are nearest rank over every request, failures included. A run with client_saturated above zero fails its own check.
Recovery time is the event to the last failed request. Replica restore time is polled from the container list at 200 ms resolution.
Deploy latency is Deploy to the first answer from the new version through the ingress, and includes the stability window the deploy gate waits for.
With repeat above 1 every run is kept and listed; nothing is averaged or dropped.
caveats: NOT Linux production numbers: the host is darwin and Docker runs inside a virtual machine, so container, network and disk paths differ from a Linux server.
Docker Desktop engine: the container runtime is a shared virtual machine, not a native Linux Docker.
Load generator and system under test share one machine, so they compete for CPU and the figures are a floor for throughput and a ceiling for latency.
The control plane is an in-process slice, not the shipped binary under systemd, and there is one node: nothing here covers multi-node, zones or a real network.
Host load average (1 minute) was 12.97 at start and 15.54 at end on 14 CPUs. The host was busy, so treat every latency as a noisy upper bound.
